subtopics.title: The Mother Graphs — Sine, Cosine and Tangent

questions.question: The amplitude of a wave is measured:
options: From a trough to a peak
From the middle line out to a peak
From the y-axis to the first zero

questions.question: Cosine differs from sine in that cosine:
options: Opens at its maximum instead of at zero

questions.question: Tangent has vertical asymptotes because:
options: Sine is zero at those angles
The cosine underneath heads to zero as the angle nears 90°

questions.question: The period of the mother tangent graph is:

subtopics.title: Amplitude and Vertical Shift — the Work of a and q

questions.question: y = 3 sin x − 1 swings between:
options: 2 and −4, around a middle line at −1

questions.question: A sketched wave has maximum 2 and minimum −4. Its q is:
options: −1 — the average of maximum and minimum

questions.question: The same wave's amplitude is:
options: 3 — half of the total swing from −4 up to 2

questions.question: A negative a changes:
options: The amplitude to a negative number
Where maxima and minima fall — the wave flips, but amplitude stays positive

subtopics.title: Changing the Period — the Effect of k

questions.question: The period of y = sin 3x is:
The period of y = cos(x/2) is:
options: 720° — one lazy half-wave fits in the standard window

questions.question: The asymptotes of y = tan 3x stand at:
options: 30° plus multiples of 60° — the walls compress with everything else

questions.question: k changes:
options: The period only — heights and middle line stay untouched

questions.question: y = sin(x − 45°) starts its climb at:
options: x = 45° — where the bracket equals zero

questions.question: The full relationship between cosine and sine is:
options: Cosine is sine shifted 90° to the left
Cosine is sine reflected in the x-axis
Cosine is sine with double the period
Cosine is sine with half the amplitude

questions.question: For y = 2 sin(x − 30°), the y-intercept check at x = 0 gives:
options: −1 — two times sine of minus thirty

questions.question: The reliable order for a combined sketch is:
The two measurements that pin down any heartbeat wave are:
options: How tall it swings (amplitude) and how long one beat lasts (period)

questions.question: A wave with top 2 and bottom −4 has middle line and half-swing:
options: Middle −1, half-swing 3 — so the wave is 3 sin x − 1

questions.question: Tangent could never appear on a heart monitor because:
options: It has no peaks — it runs wall to wall, infinitely low to infinitely high

questions.question: Sine of 3x is the same song:
options: Played at triple speed — a full verse in 120°

questions.question: The fast-forward button can never change:
options: The number of cycles in the window
The volume — sin 3x still swings between 1 and −1

questions.question: A window of 360° showing three complete waves means:
The complete three-step reading recipe for a wave picture is:
options: Middle line gives q, half-swing gives a, cycles-per-window gives k
Maximum, then minimum, then maximum again

questions.question: The horizontal shift changes:
options: Only when the song starts — not its speed or volume

questions.question: To find any shift, refuse the sign and ask:
options: How many cycles fit the window
Where the bracket equals zero — that is the wave's new starting point

questions.question: Sine of (x + 90°) opens at a peak, falls through zero, bottoms out, returns. It is:
options: Cosine, note for note — sine with an early start

questions.question: The musician's closing check on y = 2 sin(x − 30°) is:
options: Measure the period with a ruler
Play the first note: at x = 0 the equation gives −1, so the curve must cut the y-axis there
